title: Does ivE-Security Imply Knowledge of Tags?
summary: A10–A12 provide authenticity under the knowledge-of-tags assumption; whether ivE-security implies that assumption remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the $A_{10}$, $A_{11}$, and $A_{12}$ schemes, determine whether the knowledge-of-tags assumption used to establish authenticity is implied by ivE-security. These three schemes are known to provide authenticity under this additional security assumption, but it is unresolved whether ivE-security entails the knowledge-of-tags assumption.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption security for the A10, A11, and A12 generic-composition schemes.
assumptions: The knowledge-of-tags assumption is used to establish authenticity.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether ivE-security implies the knowledge-of-tags assumption for A10, A11, and A12.

progress.summary: The source proves authenticity for A10–A12 under the knowledge-of-tags assumption and explicitly states that its implication by ivE-security is unknown.
citation_labels: Chanathip Namprempre et al., Reconsidering Generic Composition
